title: Run rule for printing a bit
statement: Let $P$ be a counter program on a binary input $x$, with label $\ell$, destination label $\ell'$, bit $b$, register assignment $\rho$, and input position $p$. If the instruction at $\ell$ prints $b$ and then goes to $\ell'$, then for every output string $o$, within at most one step the program reaches $\ell'$ with registers $\rho$, input position $p$, and output $o$ followed by $b$.
hypotheses_covered: The instruction at $\ell$ prints bit $b$ and goes to $\ell'$
The claim holds for every initial output string $o$
replaced:
Let $P$ be a counter program on a binary input $x$ and $\ell$ a label whose
instruction is $\mathsf{out}(b, \ell')$, ``print the bit $b$, then go to
$\ell'$''.  Then for all registers $\rho$ and input positions $p$, from label
$\ell$ with registers $\rho$ and $p$ symbols read the program reaches label
$\ell'$ with registers $\rho$ and $p$ symbols read within one step, appending the
single bit $b$ to its output.
